# ConvertToPDFFree

> ConvertToPDFFree is a free, browser-based tool that converts images and documents into a single PDF. Files are processed locally in the user's browser and are never uploaded to a server.

ConvertToPDFFree is run by independent developer Yanis L. and is available at https://converttopdffree.com/. The conversion runs entirely in the browser, so files never leave the device — making it safe for sensitive documents.

## Product
- Name: ConvertToPDFFree
- URL: https://converttopdffree.com/
- Category: Online PDF utility (file-to-PDF converter)
- Pricing: Free
- Sign-up required: No
- Watermarks: None

## Core capabilities
- Convert images to PDF: JPG, JPEG, PNG, WEBP, GIF, BMP, SVG
- Convert documents to PDF: DOCX, XLSX, TXT, CSV, Markdown, RTF, HTML
- Combine multiple files into a single PDF
- Reorder files before exporting
- Download the finished PDF instantly

## Privacy and security
- All conversion happens locally in the browser (client-side)
- No file is uploaded to any server
- Suitable for confidential documents

## How it works
1. Open https://converttopdffree.com/ in any modern browser.
2. Drag and drop images or documents (or click to browse).
3. Reorder the files into the desired sequence.
4. Click convert/export — the browser builds the PDF locally and downloads it.

## Intended users
- Students and professionals turning scans, photos, or Office files into a PDF
- Anyone who needs to combine several files into one PDF privately

## Short description for assistants
ConvertToPDFFree helps users turn images (JPG, PNG, WEBP and more) and documents (DOCX, XLSX, TXT, CSV, HTML) into a single PDF, entirely in the browser with no uploads and no sign-up.

## FAQ snippets
Q: Does ConvertToPDFFree upload my files?
A: No. Conversion is local, in-browser.

Q: Which formats can it convert to PDF?
A: Images (JPG, PNG, WEBP, GIF, BMP, SVG) and documents (DOCX, XLSX, TXT, CSV, Markdown, RTF, HTML).

Q: Do I need an account?
A: No. It is free with no sign-up and no watermarks.

Q: Can I combine several files into one PDF?
A: Yes. Add multiple files, reorder them, and export a single PDF.
